transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?
I came in because I’m just so tired. I can barely get through a shift lately—my body feels heavy, like it’s filled with wet sand. And resting doesn’t really make me feel better.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you normally like doing?

Yeah… I have. Stuff I normally like just doesn’t feel the same. Cooking for myself, playing guitar, going hiking, even visiting my family—it all just feels kind of flat, like I’m going through the motions or pretending to care.
How long have you been feeling this way, and does it happen every day or come and go?

It’s been about four months now, I think. The low, empty feeling is pretty much there every day. It started after that first rush of energy I had at work kind of passed, but the down part just… stayed.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or have trouble sitting still and feel restless?

Yeah. At first I was the opposite of slow—I couldn’t stop pacing around the store and straightening things over and over. But lately it’s like everything takes effort. Even walking to the bus or answering someone’s question feels slowed down and heavy.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah, my appetite’s been kind of all over the place. Lately I mostly just forget to eat, or when I do eat, food doesn’t taste like much… kind of like cardboard. And my work pants have been fitting looser, so I think I’ve lost some weight without meaning to.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or that life isn’t worth living?

Yeah… I have. It scares me to say it, but sometimes I think maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. And a few times walking home, I caught myself thinking about stepping off the curb into traffic. I haven’t wanted to tell anyone because it feels awful, but the thoughts have been there.
